labels.claim: Kerr extends the logic: family regression under stress follows the same pattern, and a paper wasp colony he describes split into two nests only after sustained internal conflict made the original homeostasis untenable — regression as both symptom and trigger for reorganization.

labels.claim: Kent Berridge's research at Michigan then establishes that wanting (dopamine-driven motivation) and liking (opioid- and endocannabinoid-driven pleasure) are produced by distinct, dissociable brain subsystems — a finding Kerr connects to clinical observations about compulsive togetherness-seeking and the gap between stated and pursued goals.
labels.label: WRONG
source_quotes: That's where Bowen theory comes in.
labels.note: Kerr never connects wanting/liking to clinical observations about compulsive togetherness-seeking or stated vs pursued goals; the claim credits him with it.

labels.claim: Kerr's point is structural: correct ideas can face organized institutional resistance for centuries, and Bowen theory may currently occupy the Aristarchus-to-Copernicus phase — valid but not yet dominant.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT
source_quotes: What will the course of Bowen Family Systems Theory be like? I suspect it will not take 2000 years to dominate the public consciousness, as did heliocentrism
religion was very much tied up in this as well
labels.note: As D1.

labels.claim: Kerr draws an explicit parallel to Bowen's individuality and togetherness life forces, noting that when cells are freed from multicellular coordination they reacquire ancestral proliferative and mobile properties — a regression to earlier autonomous operating modes that he links to the regression Bowen described in families under sustained stress.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT
source_quotes: I think that's a very sharp parallel with individuality and togetherness.
And I would take it out to the family level as well, of course.
labels.note: Supported; 'families under sustained stress' is framing.

labels.claim: Kerr notes that advertising targets wanting rather than liking, and that barriers can intensify wanting while reducing liking — observations with direct implications for understanding compulsive togetherness-seeking and overfunctioning.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT
source_quotes: The focus of advertising is to stimulate not your enjoyment of an item, but your desire to have it.
We sometimes want it more while liking it less.
labels.note: Both observations are Kerr's; the 'implications for togetherness-seeking and overfunctioning' clause is the writer's, not credited to Kerr. Could be W4 (overfunctioning is not in the talk).

labels.claim: Moving the electrode millimeters in any direction eliminated the effect.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT

labels.claim: He frames this as an open question for Bowen theorists, suggesting that the neural and biological evidence reviewed points toward answers that extend well beyond the boundaries of the human species.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT
source_quotes: A question for Bowen theorists.
I think we can safely say that the answers extend beyond the boundaries of our species
labels.note: The species remark ends the first presentation, not the closing question.

labels.claim: Kerr also presents the systems biology work of Italian philosopher of science Marta Bertoloso, whose book *Philosophy of Cancer* he finds strikingly parallel to Bowen theory.
labels.label: WRONG
source_quotes: And I was trying to think about how Maria Bertoloso would say that.
labels.note: 'Marta' is not in the source; Kerr gives no first name and a participant says 'Maria'. True in the world, W1 by the approved policy.

labels.claim: Bertoloso's central claim—that genes are "only like the keys on a piano; although they are essential, it is the context that makes the music"—resonates with Bowen's shift from intrapsychic traits to functioning position within a relationship system.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT
source_quotes: Genes are only like the keys on a piano. Although they are essential, it is the context that makes the music.
He switched from character traits to functioning position.
labels.note: 'central claim' for 'my favorite quote'; the link to Bowen's shift is the writer's.

labels.claim: An email update confirms the daughter is enrolled, working at a bar, making friends, and functioning off psychiatric medications, which she reports had dulled her feelings and correlated with increased self-harm.

She seems to be functioning better off the medications.

labels.claim: The speaker draws explicit parallels throughout: the identified patient in a family corresponds to the tissue niche where cancer emerges; multi-generational transmission of chronic anxiety corresponds to the systemic perturbation that prevents tissue regeneration; and the non-reductionist, bidirectional causal model Noble diagrams—with arrows flowing both up and down from genes through organism—maps onto Bowen theory's insistence that the family system must be added at the top of that chain.
labels.label: WRONG
source_quotes: looking at that individual in the context of the family in this recent history and also as you know multi-generationally. So there's a tremendous number of parallels here.

labels.note: Kerr parallels the niche with the family context, not the identified patient; the perturbation-to-multigenerational mapping is the writer's; both presented as his explicit parallels. Could be N2.

labels.claim: His mother, convinced Billy was fragile, had protected him intensely, and this protection—rooted in the mother's anxiety rather than Billy's actual condition—became the crucible in which Billy's illness developed.
labels.label: NOT QUITE RIGHT

labels.note: Kerr tells it as the projection process; 'the crucible in which the illness developed' is the writer's causal framing. Could be W4 (Kerr stresses not blaming the mother).

labels.claim: This process is not malicious; it feels like love and protection to those generating it.

labels.claim: This connection operates at every scale: the individual body, the nuclear family, the multigenerational system, and society itself.

labels.note: Connects topics the talk covers.
